newsitem.title: FRANCE: Cook says UK should join EMU if it success - paper.
newsitem.headline: Cook says UK should join EMU if it success - paper.

text.p: Britain should join the planned European single currency if it turns out to be a success, Foreign Secretary Robin Cook said in an interview published in the afternoon daily Le Monde on Wednesday.

"If monetary union is launched and it is a success, I have already said that in the long term Great Britain should join," the newspaper quoted Cook as saying. He said it "would not be appropriate at this stage to fix a specific date as an objective (for joining)."

One of the attractive aspects to monetary union, due to go into effect on January 1, 1999, was that it "would eliminate speculation among our currencies. That would give a lot of security to our exporters," Cook told the paper.

"But if we have a single currency with a central bank that decides monetary policy, we need to strengthen the Ecofin council (of finance ministers) to ensure this monetary policy goes hand in hand with an economic strategy for jobs, growth, and production," he said.
He also expressed reservations about how to reconcile the "very different degrees of development" among European countries under a single currency.

The new Labour goverment under Prime Minister Tony Blair has said it wants a "fresh start" in its dealings with Europe after 18 years of Conservative rule marked by hostility toward Brussels. The Labour party has said that any decision to scrap sterling would have to be endorsed by a referendum.
